note: The mechanical properties of the candidate ledger, one scenario per rule. `base` is a well-formed call — one carried candidate, one fresh observation of it — and each scenario shallow-merges its `overrides` onto it, so a scenario's diff is exactly the thing being tested. Every figure is illustrative. The shape is `fixtures/ledger.json`'s: base + scenarios[{name, why, overrides, expect}]. ⛔ The ledger written here and the catalyst register written by `lib/ledger.mjs` are two documents joined by catalystIds[] and never merged.

candidates.hypothesis: 억눌린 규제 단가가 정상화되면 미수금 잔액이 3분기부터 감소로 돌아선다.

scenarios.name: a-carried-candidate-is-resumed-and-not-duplicated
scenarios.why: The control. The same name found a second way is one row with two discovery paths — never a second row, and therefore never a second proposal on one name.

scenarios.name: an-unread-ledger-is-data-missing-and-writes-nothing
scenarios.why: `undefined` is nobody having read the key. A run that cannot see its own roster cannot tell a new name from one it has been researching for a month, and writing either down would be a guess in a durable record.

scenarios.name: a-ledger-read-and-empty-seeds
scenarios.why: `null` is a positive statement: the key was read and holds nothing. It re-seeds, which is what stops the key ever locking itself — the failure #222 found next door, where one malformed write made a key permanently unreadable by its own owner.

scenarios.name: a-hand-written-blob-degrades-rather-than-locking-the-key
scenarios.why: The pre-#305 writes carry descriptive fields and no schemaVersion. Carrying less history is never carrying wrong history, and the sibling keys are named rather than copied — the byte budget measures this document's own fields.

scenarios.name: a-schema-version-this-code-does-not-know-is-refused
scenarios.why: A writer this code has never seen may have shaped its rows in a way this one would silently drop, and dropping history is the failure the whole file guards against.

scenarios.name: a-ledger-written-after-as-of-is-refused
scenarios.why: A document from a later run can hold only past-dated rows and still carry that run's judgement backwards. The per-row check does not catch it, which is why it is checked on the document.

scenarios.name: evidence-ids-cannot-be-dropped-on-restatement
scenarios.why: The row came back without the id that put it in the ledger. The carried value wins, the id is reinstated, and the run stops rather than proceeding on a record that reads clean — a laundered record is worse than a missing one.

scenarios.name: a-terminal-state-cannot-be-restated-away
scenarios.why: The carried record says excluded and this run handed back researching. A state that was reached is left where it is; moving it is an explicit transition with a reason, not a restatement.

scenarios.name: an-excluded-candidate-re-enters-only-on-a-reason-and-new-evidence
scenarios.why: A name this desk refused comes back because something changed. Re-reading what excluded it is not that something, and an extension argued from the same evidence is the position arguing with the record.

scenarios.name: the-same-re-entry-with-a-reason-and-a-new-id-is-accepted
scenarios.why: The other half of the rule above, so what is being asserted is the reason and the new evidence rather than the transition itself.

transitions.reentryReason: The ministry published the effective date that was missing when this name was excluded

scenarios.name: an-illegal-transition-is-refused
scenarios.why: The state machine is the record. discovered does not lead to proposed, because the two states in between are the work.

scenarios.name: a-rule-version-change-is-flagged-and-never-migrated
scenarios.why: A candidate admitted under one gate is not a candidate under the next one. It comes back exactly as stored, marked for re-evaluation, with both versions named. Re-stamping it here would make every gate change retroactively true of every name already in the ledger.

scenarios.name: a-copied-price-series-is-refused
scenarios.why: Prices, bars, filing bodies, holdings, cash and open proposals are re-read from the host every run. A private copy is a second source of truth that nothing reconciles and that reads exactly like a fresh one when it is a month old — #305 puts this in the scope-out list by name.

scenarios.name: a-copied-holding-is-refused-too
scenarios.why: The other family: the account. A quantity, a weight or an average cost in a research roster is the book restated where nothing will ever reconcile it.

scenarios.name: a-catalyst-id-the-register-does-not-carry-is-refused
scenarios.why: The two documents are joined by this key and by nothing else, so a link that does not resolve is a candidate resting on a row nobody can read.

scenarios.name: an-unread-register-leaves-the-link-unverified-rather-than-good
scenarios.why: The register was not passed, so the ids could not be resolved. The link is carried unchanged and is not claimed to be good — which is the same three-state discipline the rest of this package applies to every limit it reads.

scenarios.name: a-failed-range-that-failed-again-counts-the-attempt
scenarios.why: The attempts count is the record of how long a hole has been open. A run that re-writes the entry from scratch resets it, which is the same failure as a delay count that restarts — one document over.

scenarios.name: a-hypothesis-longer-than-one-sentence-is-refused
scenarios.why: A roster holds one sentence. Longer than that is research prose, and research prose belongs in the proposal where a person reads it rather than in a durable index that has a byte budget.

scenarios.name: more-than-eight-evidence-ids-is-a-citation-store
scenarios.why: Past eight the roster has stopped being a roster. The ids that matter are the ones the proposal actually rests on, and the rest are in Evidence where they belong.

idempotency.why: #305 asks that a repeated run produce no duplicate ledger row and no duplicate proposal. The mechanical half is that this operation is a pure function of its inputs and that feeding its own output back in is a fixed point: the second run's ledger equals the first's except for the instant it was written, which is the same instant because asOf is the same.
